assumptions.choice: All percentage caps (1% risk, 70%/30% module limits, 90% overall limit) are computed against current portfolio value (self.broker.getvalue()) at signal time, not the fixed initial cash.
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'capital' repeatedly without specifying fixed vs. dynamic basis; mark-to-market equity is the standard risk-management convention.

assumptions.choice: Module 1 and Module 2 are tracked as independent logical share-count sleeves (m1_size, m2_core_size) layered on the one aggregate backtrader position for the single AAPL feed; exits use explicit self.sell(size=...) for only the relevant module's shares instead of self.close().
assumptions.reason: The harness supplies a single data feed for a single asset, so the two conceptually separate capital pools must share one broker position; self.close() would incorrectly liquidate both modules at once, so canonical default #2 is overridden with explicit sizing.

assumptions.choice: Two independent pending-order attributes (order_m1, order_m2) are each reset in notify_order on Completed/Canceled/Margin/Rejected, rather than one shared guard.
assumptions.reason: Modules act on independent signals/capital and must not block each other while one has an order in flight.

assumptions.choice: All entry/exit thresholds (trend, RSI, band touches, stop/target/trailing levels) are evaluated against the bar's Close; qualifying signals are submitted as plain market orders, filled by backtrader at the next bar's Open.
assumptions.reason: Spec explicitly requires next-bar entries for Module 1; applying the same Close-based check / next-open-fill convention uniformly to all other conditions (including exits) avoids mixing intrabar assumptions with the stated next-bar rule, given only OHLCV is available.

assumptions.choice: When stop, take-profit/mid-band, and time-exit conditions are simultaneously true on one bar, priority is stop-loss > take-profit/mid-band > time exit.
assumptions.reason: Spec lists all three exit types but does not state a priority; risk containment is given precedence by convention.

assumptions.choice: ATR(14) at the signal bar is captured when the entry order is submitted; once notify_order confirms the fill, stop = fill_price - 1*ATR_at_signal and target = fill_price + 0.7*ATR_at_signal.
assumptions.reason: The actual next-bar-open fill price is unknown at signal time, so bracket-order price pre-computation isn't possible; anchoring the ATR-based levels to the confirmed fill price is the closest literal reading.

assumptions.choice: The entry fill bar counts as bar 0; the time exit triggers once (current_bar_index - entry_bar_index) >= 10.
assumptions.reason: Spec states 'max hold: 10 bars' without a counting convention; this is the natural zero-indexed reading.

assumptions.choice: Both base entry and add orders deploy the maximum share count fitting within whichever is tighter of the remaining 30% module-2 budget and the remaining 90% total-capital budget at signal time, with no fixed capital split reserved between base entry and later adds.
assumptions.reason: Spec caps module 2 at 30%/90% overall but never specifies how much of that budget a single base entry vs. a later add should consume; an available-room sizing mirrors Module 1's room-based approach and is consistent across both modules.

assumptions.choice: The 'Add' rule (10% pullback from 20-day high, lower-band touch, RSI 35-45) only fires when a core position already exists (m2_core_size > 0); with no core, only the 'Base entry' rule can open the position.
assumptions.reason: The spec presents Add as a scaling mechanism under an already-established core ('adding on pullbacks'); requiring an existing core is the more literal reading of 'Add' versus 'Base entry'.

assumptions.choice: A fixed 15% of the current core size (within the stated 10-20% range) is sold per partial profit-taking event, truncated to whole shares.
assumptions.reason: Spec gives a range without pinning an exact value; the midpoint is chosen and declared.

assumptions.choice: The 20-day high used for the 10% pullback Add trigger is bt.indicators.Highest on the data's High price (period 20), not Close.
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'the 20-day high' without specifying which OHLC field; highest High over the lookback is the standard price-action reading.

assumptions.choice: 'MACD > 0' is read as the raw MACD line (fast EMA(12) - slow EMA(26)) value, not the signal line or histogram.
assumptions.reason: Spec names 'MACD > 0' without qualifying which MACD component; the MACD line itself is the standard default referent.

assumptions.choice: 'Touches or is below the lower band' / 'touches the upper band' use <= / >= respectively; 'return to the middle band' is interpreted directionally per context: Module 1 TP and Module 2 base-entry pullback use price approaching the middle band from below/above their respective prior extremes, and Module 2 buyback (after a partial sell near the upper band) uses price falling back down to <= the middle band.
assumptions.reason: Spec's 'touches' and 'return to' phrasing doesn't state strict inequality direction in every instance; directions are chosen to match the natural price path implied by each rule's context.
